newsitem.title: UK: Buyers back away from higher UK meals prices.
newsitem.headline: Buyers back away from higher UK meals prices.

text.p: Buyers back away from higher prices on the UK meals and feeds market on Friday.
Sellers marked up prices following a sharp turn around in Chicago futures during project A trading on news that a sale of Brazilian soybeans to a U.S. firm had fallen through.
Higher opening prices in Chicago during Friday made it unlikely that any business would be done.
U.S. prices rose on rumours that Brazil may impose tax on exports of soybeans.
"I don't think the Brazilian are going to do the Americans any favours like that," said one broker.
"They wheel this story out every so often, but it's not happened yet," said another.
High protein soymeal was one to five stg up ex-mill and 2.50 to four stg higher from the stores.
Rapemeal from the Erith mill was one to two stg down while Liverpool and Hull offers were unchanged.
Brokers would not quote resellers for Erith material as they were not competitive.
"The mill has cut its prices and made the resellers uncompetitive," said one broker.
